**Seminar**

## Exercise 10.1. Build the matrix from three hints

Work in the first approximation: $U_{e3}=0$, the atmospheric mixing angle
is close to $45^\circ$, and the matrix may be chosen real.

1. For high-energy solar neutrinos take
   $P_{ee}\simeq1/3$. For an adiabatic exit from the Sun this gives
   $|U_{e2}|^2\simeq1/3$. Using the normalization of the electron row,
   fill in $|U_{e1}|^2$ and $|U_{e3}|^2$.
2. Atmospheric disappearance is described in the leading approximation by the depth
   $4|U_{\mu3}|^2(1-|U_{\mu3}|^2)\simeq1$. Find $|U_{\mu3}|^2$.
   Fill in $|U_{\tau3}|^2$ from the normalization of the third column.
3. Choose the same signs for $U_{\mu3}$ and $U_{\tau3}$. What does the
   orthogonality of the second and third columns say about the relation between
   $U_{\mu2}$ and $U_{\tau2}$? Normalize the second column and fill in
   $|U_{\mu2}|^2$, $|U_{\tau2}|^2$.
4. Use the normalizations of the two remaining rows. Show that

   $$
   |U_0|^2=
   \begin{pmatrix}
   2/3&1/3&0\\
   1/6&1/3&1/2\\
   1/6&1/3&1/2
   \end{pmatrix}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-manual-matrix}

5. Choose the signs of the elements so that the resulting real matrix
   $U_0$ satisfies $U_0^{\mathsf T}U_0=I$. Write out all three ones
   and all six zeros in the product.
6. Which entry does the reactor result $|U_{e3}|^2\simeq0.0225$ change
   first? Explain which conclusions of the approximate matrix remain
   qualitatively correct. Can this construction be used to independently check
   unitarity, if it was used at every step?

## Exercise 10.2. How to read the PMNS matrix

Use the standard factorization

$$
U=R_{23}U_{13}(\delta)R_{12}.
$$ {#eq-ex10-001}

1. Multiply the matrices and obtain the first row and the third column of $U$.
2. Prove the relations

   $$
   |U_{e3}|=\sin\theta_{13},
   \qquad
   \frac{|U_{e2}|}{|U_{e1}|}=\tan\theta_{12},
   \qquad
   \frac{|U_{\mu3}|}{|U_{\tau3}|}=\tan\theta_{23}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-002}

3. For the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit point with normal ordering use

   $$
   \sin^2\theta_{12}=0.3088,
   \quad
   \sin^2\theta_{23}=0.470,
   \quad
   \sin^2\theta_{13}=0.02248
   $$ {#eq-ex10-003}

   and compute
   $|U_{e1}|$, $|U_{e2}|$, $|U_{e3}|$, $|U_{\mu3}|$ and $|U_{\tau3}|$.
4. Explain why the phase $\delta$ becomes unobservable at
   $s_{13}=0$.
5. An arbitrary unitary matrix $3\times3$ contains three angles and six
   phases. Count how many phases can be removed by rephasing the fields in
   the Dirac case.
6. For the Majorana case set

   $$
   \widetilde U
   =U\operatorname{diag}
   \left(1,e^{i\alpha_{21}/2},e^{i\alpha_{31}/2}\right).
   $$ {#eq-ex10-004}

   Show that the additional phases cancel in the product
   $\widetilde U_{\beta i}\widetilde U_{\alpha i}^*$ and therefore do not enter the
   oscillation probabilities.

**Homework**

## Exercise 10.3. General three-flavor probability

For three active neutrinos

$$
|\nu_\alpha\rangle
=\sum_{i=1}^3U_{\alpha i}^*|\nu_i\rangle.
$$ {#eq-ex10-005}

1. Carry out the evolution of the mass components and obtain the ultrarelativistic
   amplitude

   $$
   \mathcal A_{\alpha\to\beta}(L,E)
   =\sum_iU_{\beta i}U_{\alpha i}^*
   \exp\!\left(-i\frac{m_i^2L}{2E}\right).
   $$ {#eq-ex10-006}

2. Square the amplitude and obtain a double sum over $i,j$.
3. Combine the terms $(i,j)$ and $(j,i)$, introduce

   $$
   X_{\alpha\beta}^{ij}
   =U_{\alpha i}^*U_{\beta i}
    U_{\alpha j}U_{\beta j}^*,
   \qquad
   \Delta_{ij}=\frac{\Delta m_{ij}^2L}{4E},
   $$ {#eq-ex10-007}

   and derive the general probability formula in terms of
   $\operatorname{Re}X^{ij}$ and $\operatorname{Im}X^{ij}$.
4. Obtain the formula for the survival probability $P_{\alpha\to\alpha}$.
5. Using the unitarity $U$, prove

   $$
   \sum_\beta P_{\alpha\to\beta}=1
   $$ {#eq-ex10-008}

   and show that for $L=0$
   $P_{\alpha\to\beta}=\delta_{\alpha\beta}$.
6. Show how the general formula reduces to the two-flavor one if one
   mass component does not participate.
7. Prove

   $$
   \Delta m_{31}^2=\Delta m_{32}^2+\Delta m_{21}^2
   $$ {#eq-ex10-009}

   and explain why only two oscillation frequencies are independent.
8. Perform the replacement $m_i^2\to m_i^2+C$. Show that the amplitude acquires
   only an overall phase factor, while the probability does not change.
9. Which experiments, unlike oscillations, are sensitive to the absolute
   scale of neutrino masses?

## Exercise 10.4. CP violation and the Jarlskog invariant

1. Show that for antineutrinos the oscillation amplitude is obtained
   by the replacement $U\to U^*$.
2. Using the general three-flavor probability, obtain

   $$
   A_{\alpha\beta}^{\mathrm{CP}}
   =P(\nu_\alpha\to\nu_\beta)
   -P(\bar\nu_\alpha\to\bar\nu_\beta)
   =4\sum_{i>j}\operatorname{Im}X_{\alpha\beta}^{ij}
   \sin2\Delta_{ij}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-010}

3. Prove that $A_{\alpha\alpha}^{\mathrm{CP}}=0$ in vacuum.
4. For the quartet

   $$
   J_{\mathrm{CP}}
   =\operatorname{Im}
   \left(U_{e2}^*U_{\mu2}U_{e1}U_{\mu1}^*\right)
   $$ {#eq-ex10-011}

   check the invariance under rephasing of the rows and columns of the mixing
   matrix.
5. From the standard PMNS parametrization obtain

   $$
   J_{\mathrm{CP}}
   =\frac18
   \sin2\theta_{12}\sin2\theta_{23}\sin2\theta_{13}
   \cos\theta_{13}\sin\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-012}

6. Using $\Delta_{31}=\Delta_{32}+\Delta_{21}$ and trigonometric
   identities, derive

   $$
   A_{e\mu}^{\mathrm{CP}}
   =16J_{\mathrm{CP}}
   \sin\Delta_{21}\sin\Delta_{32}\sin\Delta_{31}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-013}

7. List all the conditions under which the vacuum CP asymmetry vanishes.
   Why is there no fundamental CP violation in the two-flavor vacuum
   model?
8. For the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit point with normal ordering use

   $$
   \theta_{12}=33.76^\circ,
   \quad
   \theta_{23}=43.29^\circ,
   \quad
   \theta_{13}=8.62^\circ,
   \quad
   \delta_{\mathrm{CP}}=212^\circ
   $$ {#eq-ex10-014}

   and compute $J_{\mathrm{CP}}$.
9. Estimate $A_{e\mu}^{\mathrm{CP}}$ at the first atmospheric maximum,
   defined by the condition $\Delta_{31}=\pi/2$. Use

   $$
   \Delta m_{21}^2=7.537\cdot10^{-5}~\mathrm{eV}^2,
   \qquad
   \Delta m_{31}^2=2.511\cdot10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV}^2.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-015}

   Why is the asymmetry additionally suppressed by the smallness of the solar phase?

## Exercise 10.5. Numerical lab of three flavors

Write a program in Python, Julia, or Mathematica that computes vacuum
oscillations of three active neutrinos. For Python you can use the
[template](https://neutrinohit.github.io/neutrinophysics/introduction/ru/exercises/assets/09_vacuum_oscillations/three_flavor_starter.en.py).

Use the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit point with normal ordering:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin^2\theta_{12}&=0.3088,&
\sin^2\theta_{23}&=0.470,&
\sin^2\theta_{13}&=0.02248,\\
\Delta m_{21}^2&=7.537\cdot10^{-5}~\mathrm{eV}^2,&
\Delta m_{31}^2&=2.511\cdot10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV}^2,&
\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}&=212^\circ.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ex10-016}

1. Construct the PMNS matrix in the standard parametrization and numerically check
   $U^\dagger U=I$.
2. Implement the amplitude $\mathcal A_{\alpha\to\beta}$. If the rows
   denote the final flavor $\beta$ and the columns the initial flavor $\alpha$,
   then in matrix form

   $$
   \mathcal A
   =U\operatorname{diag}(e^{-i\phi_i})U^\dagger,
   \qquad
   \phi_i=2(1.267)\frac{m_i^2[\mathrm{eV}^2]L[\mathrm{km}]}
                              {E[\mathrm{GeV}]}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-017}

   One can set $m_1^2=0$, since the overall mass is not observable.
3. Compute the probability matrix $P_{\beta\alpha}=|\mathcal A_{\beta\alpha}|^2$.
4. Automatically check

   $$
   P_{\beta\alpha}(0)=\delta_{\beta\alpha},
   \qquad
   \sum_\beta P_{\beta\alpha}=1
   $$ {#eq-ex10-018}

   with a numerical accuracy no worse than $10^{-12}$.
5. For the initial $\nu_\mu$ plot $P_{\mu\to e}$,
   $P_{\mu\to\mu}$ and $P_{\mu\to\tau}$ as functions of $L/E$ in the range
   $0\leq L/E\leq2000~\mathrm{km/GeV}$.
6. Repeat the calculation for antineutrinos, replacing $U\to U^*$, and plot
   $P_{\mu\to e}-\overline P_{\mu\to e}$.
7. Repeat the comparison at $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}=0$ and explain the result.
8. Add the same number $C$ to all $m_i^2$ and numerically check
   that the probabilities do not change.
9. By scanning over $L/E$, find the point of the maximal vacuum
   difference $P_{\mu\to e}-\overline P_{\mu\to e}$ in absolute value in the indicated range.
10. Represent the triple of probabilities

    $$
    (P_{\alpha\to e},P_{\alpha\to\mu},P_{\alpha\to\tau})
    $$ {#eq-ex10-019}

    as a trajectory inside the probability triangle. Why can the trajectory not
    leave the triangle?
11. In item 1 the matrix is unitary by construction. What independent
    experimental normalizations and channels would be needed to check
    unitarity without fixing it in the parametrization in advance?

In a real long-baseline experiment the comparison of neutrinos and antineutrinos
is also modified by matter. In this exercise only the vacuum part needs to be computed.

## Exercise 10.6. What the moduli of the matrix know about the phase $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}$

In the standard parametrization the elements of the first column are

$$
U_{e1}=c_{12}c_{13},
\qquad
U_{\mu1}=-s_{12}c_{23}-c_{12}s_{23}s_{13}e^{i\delta},
\qquad
U_{\tau1}=s_{12}s_{23}-c_{12}c_{23}s_{13}e^{i\delta}.
$$ {#eq-ex10-020}

1. Show that

   $$
   |U_{\mu1}|^2
   =s_{12}^2c_{23}^2+c_{12}^2s_{23}^2s_{13}^2
   +2s_{12}c_{12}s_{23}c_{23}s_{13}\cos\delta,
   $$ {#eq-ex10-021}

   and obtain the analogous expression for $|U_{\tau1}|^2$.
2. Show that $|U_{\mu1}|^2+|U_{\tau1}|^2$ does not depend on $\delta$.
   Which unitarity condition does this express?
3. For the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit point with normal ordering

   $$
   \sin^2\theta_{12}=0.3088,
   \quad
   \sin^2\theta_{23}=0.470,
   \quad
   \sin^2\theta_{13}=0.02248,
   \quad
   \delta=212^\circ
   $$ {#eq-ex10-022}

   compute $|U_{\mu1}|^2$ and $|U_{\tau1}|^2$.
4. With the same angles, find the range of $|U_{\mu1}|$ as $\delta$ runs
   from $0$ to $360^\circ$. The global analysis gives the $3\sigma$
   interval from $0.259$ to $0.498$ for $|U_{\mu1}|$ and from $0.810$ to
   $0.834$ for $|U_{e1}|$. Why are the entries of the $\mu$ and $\tau$ rows
   known much worse than those of the electron row?
5. Prove that the phases $\delta$ and $360^\circ-\delta$ give the same
   matrix of moduli $|U_{\alpha i}|$. What is $J_{\mathrm{CP}}$ at
   $\delta=212^\circ$ and at $\delta=148^\circ$?
6. Show that the nine moduli determine $|J_{\mathrm{CP}}|$ but not its
   sign.

State the main conclusion: what part of the information on
$\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}$ can measurements sensitive only to $|U_{\alpha i}|$,
such as survival channels, provide, and which measurements are needed for
the sign of $\sin\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}$?

## Exercise 10.7. Two scales: when three flavors reduce to two

Use the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit point with normal ordering:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin^2\theta_{12}&=0.3088,&
\sin^2\theta_{23}&=0.470,&
\sin^2\theta_{13}&=0.02248,\\
\Delta m_{21}^2&=7.537\cdot10^{-5}~\mathrm{eV}^2,&
\Delta m_{31}^2&=2.511\cdot10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV}^2,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ex10-023}

together with

$$
P_{\alpha\to\alpha}
=1-4\sum_{i>j}|U_{\alpha i}|^2|U_{\alpha j}|^2\sin^2\Delta_{ij},
\qquad
\Delta_{ij}=1.267\,
\frac{\Delta m^2_{ij}[\mathrm{eV}^2]L[\mathrm{km}]}{E[\mathrm{GeV}]}.
$$ {#eq-ex10-024}

1. Find the ratio $\Delta m_{21}^2/\Delta m_{31}^2$. Setting
   $\Delta_{21}=0$, show that

   $$
   P_{\alpha\to\alpha}
   \simeq1-4|U_{\alpha3}|^2\left(1-|U_{\alpha3}|^2\right)
   \sin^2\Delta_{31}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-025}

2. For the electron flavor obtain
   $P_{ee}\simeq1-\sin^2 2\theta_{13}\sin^2\Delta_{31}$. For a reactor
   detector with $L=1.6~\mathrm{km}$ and $E=4~\mathrm{MeV}$ compute
   $\Delta_{21}$, $\Delta_{31}$, and the approximate and exact
   probabilities. Where is the first atmospheric disappearance maximum
   located?
3. In the same limit obtain the appearance probability

   $$
   P_{\alpha\to\beta}
   \simeq4|U_{\alpha3}|^2|U_{\beta3}|^2\sin^2\Delta_{31},
   \qquad
   \alpha\ne\beta,
   $$ {#eq-ex10-026}

   using the orthogonality of the rows $\alpha$ and $\beta$ for the sum of
   the two terms with the same phase.
4. For a $\nu_\mu$ beam with $L=295~\mathrm{km}$ and $E=0.6~\mathrm{GeV}$
   find $|U_{\mu3}|^2=s_{23}^2c_{13}^2$, the disappearance depth
   $4|U_{\mu3}|^2(1-|U_{\mu3}|^2)$, $P_{\mu\mu}$ and
   $P_{\mu e}\simeq\sin^2 2\theta_{13}\,s_{23}^2\sin^2\Delta_{31}$. Which of
   the two probabilities is sensitive to the octant of $\theta_{23}$?
   Compare $P_{\mu e}$ with the exact vacuum value at
   $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}=212^\circ$ (for example, from the program of
   Exercise 10.5) and explain the discrepancy.
5. For a reactor detector at $L=180~\mathrm{km}$ with $E=4~\mathrm{MeV}$
   find $\Delta_{31}$. Average the fast terms and show that

   $$
   P_{ee}\simeq c_{13}^4
   \left(1-\sin^2 2\theta_{12}\sin^2\Delta_{21}\right)+s_{13}^4.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-027}

   Compute this probability.
6. Which two small parameters control the accuracy of the two-flavor
   approximations? Which parameters of the matrix does each of the three
   experiments considered here measure?

State the main conclusion: why did two-flavor formulas describe individual
experiments so well, even though there are three flavors?

## Exercise 10.8. Mass ordering in the reactor antineutrino spectrum

The sign $\Delta m_{21}^2>0$ is known; the position of the third mass state
is not. Compare two options with the same angles:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{NO:}&\quad\Delta m_{31}^2=+2.511\cdot10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV}^2,
&\Delta m_{32}^2&=\Delta m_{31}^2-\Delta m_{21}^2,\\
\text{IO:}&\quad\Delta m_{32}^2=-2.511\cdot10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV}^2,
&\Delta m_{31}^2&=\Delta m_{32}^2+\Delta m_{21}^2,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ex10-028}

where $\Delta m_{21}^2=7.537\cdot10^{-5}~\mathrm{eV}^2$,
$\sin^2\theta_{12}=0.3088$, $\sin^2\theta_{13}=0.02248$. In this model
comparison the magnitudes of the two large splittings simply swap places.

1. Using $|U_{e1}|=c_{12}c_{13}$, $|U_{e2}|=s_{12}c_{13}$,
   $|U_{e3}|=s_{13}$, obtain

   $$
   P_{ee}
   =1-c_{13}^4\sin^2 2\theta_{12}\sin^2\Delta_{21}
   -\sin^2 2\theta_{13}
   \left(c_{12}^2\sin^2\Delta_{31}+s_{12}^2\sin^2\Delta_{32}\right).
   $$ {#eq-ex10-029}

2. Show that $P_{ee}$ in vacuum does not change when the signs of all
   $\Delta m_{ij}^2$ are flipped simultaneously. How, then, can the mass
   ordering enter the probability?
3. Define $\Delta_a=1.267\cdot2.511\cdot10^{-3}\,L/E$ and
   $\Delta_b=\Delta_a-\Delta_{21}$ (in practical units). Prove that

   $$
   P_{ee}^{\mathrm{NO}}-P_{ee}^{\mathrm{IO}}
   =-\sin^2 2\theta_{13}\cos2\theta_{12}\,
   \sin(\Delta_a+\Delta_b)\sin\Delta_{21}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-030}

   Find the largest possible value of
   $|P_{ee}^{\mathrm{NO}}-P_{ee}^{\mathrm{IO}}|$.
4. For $L=52.5~\mathrm{km}$ (the JUNO baseline) plot $P_{ee}(E)$ for NO
   and IO in the range $2\leq E\leq8~\mathrm{MeV}$, together with their
   difference. At what energy is the difference largest? Relate the answer
   to the first solar maximum $\Delta_{21}=\pi/2$.
5. What would happen for $\theta_{12}=45^\circ$? For $\theta_{13}=0$?
6. Estimate the period of the fast oscillations in energy near
   $E=4~\mathrm{MeV}$, $\delta E\simeq\pi E/\Delta_{31}$. What requirement on
   the energy resolution of the detector follows from it? What remains of
   the mass-ordering effect if the fast terms are averaged out?

State the main physical conclusion: how does the mass ordering show up in
vacuum if the probability is sensitive only to the magnitudes of the
splittings?

## Exercise 10.9. The unitarity triangle and the number of phases

The orthogonality of the $e$ and $\mu$ rows is written as

$$
z_1+z_2+z_3=0,
\qquad
z_i=U_{ei}U_{\mu i}^*.
$$ {#eq-ex10-031}

1. For the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit point with normal ordering

   $$
   \sin^2\theta_{12}=0.3088,
   \quad
   \sin^2\theta_{23}=0.470,
   \quad
   \sin^2\theta_{13}=0.02248,
   \quad
   \delta_{\mathrm{CP}}=212^\circ
   $$ {#eq-ex10-032}

   construct the matrix $U=R_{23}U_{13}(\delta)R_{12}$ and compute the three
   complex numbers $z_i$. Check the closure and draw the triangle in the
   complex plane.
2. Find the side lengths $|z_i|=|U_{ei}||U_{\mu i}|$. Which side is the
   shortest, and why?
3. Compute the area $S=\frac12|\operatorname{Im}(z_1^*z_2)|$ and compare it
   with $|J_{\mathrm{CP}}|/2$, where

   $$
   J_{\mathrm{CP}}
   =\frac18\sin2\theta_{12}\sin2\theta_{23}\sin2\theta_{13}
   \cos\theta_{13}\sin\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}.
   $$ {#eq-ex10-033}

4. Under the rephasing
   $U_{\alpha i}\to e^{i(\phi_\alpha-\psi_i)}U_{\alpha i}$ find how the
   $z_i$ change. Which properties of the triangle are physical, and which
   depend on the convention?
5. Repeat the calculation for $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}=0$, $180^\circ$ and
   $270^\circ$. When does the triangle degenerate into a segment? What is
   the largest area for the given angles?
6. A unitary $N\times N$ matrix has $N^2$ real parameters. Show that
   $N(N-1)/2$ of them are angles and $N(N+1)/2$ are phases. Rephasing the
   fields removes $2N-1$ phases for Dirac particles and $N$ phases for
   Majorana particles. Fill in a table of the number of physical phases for
   $N=2,3,4$.
7. Suppose the sides $|z_i|$ have been measured independently, without
   assuming unitarity. What result would be a direct sign of a violation of
   unitarity of the three-neutrino matrix?

State the main conclusion: what does the area of the unitarity triangle mean,
and why does a triangle built from the parametrization not test unitarity
itself?
